headline: YOUR NEWSPAPER WILL TALK TO YOU
deck: A story set in 2889 imagines the daily paper read aloud to 85 million subscribers, and recorded for later.
quote: Instead of being printed, the Earth Chronicle is every morning spoken to subscribers, who, in interesting conversations with reporters, statesmen, and scientists, learn the news of the day.
quote_note: From a short story. Published under Jules Verne's name; Project Gutenberg notes it is now thought to be chiefly the work of his son, Michel Verne.

quote_sources.title: In the Year 2889 — Project Gutenberg

happened: Spoken news on demand is ordinary now. Pew Research found roughly half of US adults had listened to a podcast in the past year (2023).

happened_sources.title: Podcasts as a source of news and information — Pew Research Center, 18 Apr 2023

reason: Set in 2889, but spoken, recorded news arrived about 870 years early.

headline: SUBMARINES WILL ONLY SUFFOCATE THEIR CREWS
deck: The great forecaster of the age cannot picture the submarine doing anything useful.
quote: I must confess that my imagination, in spite even of spurring, refuses to see any sort of submarine doing anything but suffocate its crew and founder at sea.

quote_sources.title: Anticipations, by H. G. Wells — Project Gutenberg eBook #19229

happened: In 1958 the nuclear submarine USS Nautilus crossed under the North Pole, fully submerged, and her crew came home to a Presidential Unit Citation.

happened_sources.title: Nautilus (SSN-571) — Naval History and Heritage Command

reason: Submarines became some of the most capable ships ever built.

headline: FLYING MACHINE MAY TAKE TEN MILLION YEARS
deck: A newspaper editorial says a machine that really flies is a very long way off.
quote: ...it might be assumed that the flying machine which will really fly might be evolved by the combined and continuous efforts of mathematicians and mechanics in from one million to ten million years...

quote_sources.title: The New York Times, 9 Oct 1903, "Flying Machines Which Do Not Fly" — Wikisource transcription
Snopes fact check

happened: Sixty-nine days later, on 17 December 1903, the Wright brothers flew the first powered, controlled aeroplane.

happened_sources.title: 1903 Wright Flyer — Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

reason: Out by about ten million years, minus 69 days.

headline: EDISON SEEKS A TELEPHONE TO THE DEAD
deck: The great inventor says he is working on an apparatus to reach those who have died.
quote: To see if it is possible for personalities which have left this earth to communicate with us.

quote_sources.title: Edison and science fiction — Thomas Edison Papers, Rutgers
Edison's Views on Life and Death — Scientific American, 30 Oct 1920

happened: Edison's archive at Rutgers says no verifiable evidence of such a device has ever been found.

happened_sources.title: Edison and science fiction — Thomas Edison Papers, Rutgers

reason: As ruled on air in the Halloween Short.

headline: ROCKETS CANNOT WORK IN A VACUUM, PAPER SCOFFS
deck: An editorial mocks Professor Goddard's plan to reach space and says he lacks high-school science.
quote: Of course, he only seems to lack the knowledge ladled out daily in high schools.
quote_note: The editorial argued a rocket needs "something better than a vacuum against which to react". It is a claim more than a forecast, but it was a claim about what rockets would never do.

quote_sources.title: FAQs about Robert H. Goddard — Clark University Archives (archived copy)

happened: On 17 July 1969, three days before the Moon walk, the Times printed: "it is now definitely established that a rocket can function in a vacuum as well as in an atmosphere. The Times regrets the error."

happened_sources.title: FAQs about Robert H. Goddard — Clark University Archives (archived copy)

reason: The paper corrected itself, 49 years later.

headline: A TELEPHONE YOU CAN CARRY IN YOUR VEST POCKET
deck: Tesla says wireless will let us see and hear each other across thousands of miles.
quote: ...through television and telephony we shall see and hear one another as perfectly as though we were face to face, despite intervening distances of thousands of miles... A man will be able to carry one in his vest pocket.
quote_note: Shortened with "..."; the full passage is in the sources.
who: Nikola Tesla, interviewed by John B. Kennedy

quote_sources.title: Snopes: Nikola Tesla predicted cellphones in 1926? (rated correctly attributed)
"When Woman is Boss" transcript — Twenty-First Century Books (archived copy)

happened: Four out of five people aged 10 and over now own a mobile phone, says the UN telecoms agency (2024).

happened_sources.title: Facts and Figures 2024: Mobile phone ownership — ITU

reason: A pocket device for seeing and hearing anyone, anywhere: that is a video call on a phone.

headline: STOCKS HAVE REACHED A PERMANENT HIGH, SAYS YALE MAN
deck: The nation's best-known economist tells a dinner audience the boom is here to stay.
quote: Stock prices have reached what looks like a permanently high plateau.
quote_note: As reported by The New York Times, 16 Oct 1929, p. 8.
where: Speech to the Purchasing Agents Association, New York

quote_sources.title: Stock Market Crash of 1929 — Federal Reserve History

happened: Within two weeks came Black Monday and Black Tuesday. By mid-1932 the Dow was 89% below its peak, and it did not get back there until November 1954.

happened_sources.title: Stock Market Crash of 1929 — Federal Reserve History

reason: The plateau lasted about nine days.

headline: ATOM POWER IS "MOONSHINE", SAYS RUTHERFORD
deck: The father of nuclear physics tells scientists not to expect energy from splitting atoms.
quote: Anyone who expects a source of power from the transformation of these atoms is talking moonshine.
quote_note: Reported in the press after his British Association speech. Newspapers printed slightly different wordings; Quote Investigator lists them.
where: British Association for the Advancement of Science, Leicester

quote_sources.title: Quote Investigator: "Talking moonshine"

happened: Nine years later, on 2 December 1942, the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction ran under a Chicago football stadium.

happened_sources.title: 10 intriguing facts about the world's first nuclear chain reaction — US Department of Energy

reason: The moonshine was flowing within a decade.

headline: FORD: THE FLYING CAR IS COMING
deck: The motor king says a combination airplane and motor car is on its way.
quote: Mark my word: A combination airplane and motor car is coming.

quote_sources.title: Henry Ford quotations — The Henry Ford

happened: Klein Vision's AirCar received a certificate of airworthiness in January 2022. It is a roadable aircraft.

happened_sources.title: AirCar receives certificate of airworthiness — The Engineer

reason: As ruled on air in Episode 1.

headline: RADIO STATIONS IN SPACE COULD COVER THE WHOLE WORLD
deck: A young engineer works out that a station 42,000 km out would hang still in the sky.
quote: A true broadcast service, giving constant field strength at all times over the whole globe would be invaluable, not to say indispensable, in a world society.
quote_note: The article shows that a body in an orbit with a radius of 42,000 km takes exactly 24 hours to go round, and so stays above the same spot.

quote_sources.title: Extra-Terrestrial Relays (Wireless World, Oct 1945) — transcription, pages 305–308
Extra-Terrestrial Relays — facsimile PDF (Universidad de los Andes space-law archive)

happened: In 1964 the geostationary satellite Syncom 3 carried TV pictures of the Tokyo Olympics to the United States. Geostationary satellites still carry the bulk of space-based communications.

happened_sources.title: Communications Satellite, Syncom — Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

reason: The orbit he described is still used for satellite TV and weather satellites.

headline: COMPUTERS MAY ONE DAY WEIGH ONLY 1½ TONS
deck: A science magazine imagines the giant electronic brains slimming down.
quote: Where a calculator like the ENIAC today is equipped with 18,000 vacuum tubes and weighs 30 tons, computers in the future may have only 1,000 vacuum tubes and perhaps weigh only 1 1/2 tons.

quote_sources.title: "A Virtual Space Odyssey; This Time, the Future Is Closer Than You Think" — The New York Times, 31 Dec 2000

happened: Laptops and desktop PCs, each vastly more powerful than ENIAC, were everywhere by 2000, as the Times noted. Today a phone in your pocket outruns it.

happened_sources.title: The New York Times, 31 Dec 2000

reason: Right that computers would shrink; wrong by roughly a factor of a thousand on how much.

headline: MACHINES WILL PASS FOR HUMAN WITHIN 50 YEARS
deck: A Manchester mathematician proposes a test: can a judge tell a computer from a person?
quote: I believe that in about fifty years' time it will be possible, to programme computers... to make them play the imitation game so well that an average interrogator will not have more than 70 per cent chance of making the right identification after five minutes of questioning.
quote_note: Shortened with "..." (it gives a storage size).

quote_sources.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence (Mind, 1950) — PDF, UMBC course archive

happened: In a 2025 study with five-minute chats, people picked the AI model GPT-4.5 as the human 73% of the time.

happened_sources.title: Jones & Bergen, "Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test" — arXiv 2503.23674 (2025)

reason: It happened, about 25 years after his "fifty years".

headline: A SPACE STATION IS "INEVITABLE AS THE RISING OF THE SUN"
deck: Wernher von Braun shows the nation a wheel-shaped station orbiting the Earth.
quote: ...as "inevitable as the rising of the sun."
quote_note: Paraphrase plus a short quoted phrase: von Braun predicted that the development of a space station orbiting Earth was as "inevitable as the rising of the sun" (New York Times TierneyLab, 2008).

quote_sources.title: Von Braun's Spaceship — The New York Times (TierneyLab), 14 Oct 2008
Von Braun, "Crossing the Last Frontier," Collier's, 22 Mar 1952 — University of Oregon digital exhibit

happened: People have lived on the International Space Station continuously since 2 November 2000.

happened_sources.title: International Space Station — NASA

reason: The station came; it is more of a laboratory than his wheel.

headline: SPACE TRAVEL IS "UTTER BILGE", SAYS ASTRONOMER ROYAL
deck: Britain's top astronomer dismisses the whole idea of going into space.
quote: ...as late as 1956, Britain's Astronomer Royal called the prospect of space travel "utter bilge."
quote_note: Paraphrase with a two-word quote, as reported by Time magazine in 1966. Time does not name him; the Astronomer Royal in 1956 was Sir Richard Woolley.

quote_sources.title: "The Futurists: Looking Toward A.D. 2000" — Time, 25 Feb 1966

happened: The next year, on 4 October 1957, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite.

happened_sources.title: Sputnik and the Dawn of the Space Age — NASA History (archived copy)

reason: Space travel began about a year later.
note: Time quote checked in the fetched Time archive page (WebFetch) on 11 Nov 2026.

headline: NAVY SHOWS EMBRYO OF A THINKING MACHINE
deck: A psychologist's computer learns by doing. The Navy expects great things.
quote: The Navy revealed the embryo of an electronic computer today that it expects will be able to walk, talk, see, write, reproduce itself and be conscious of its existence.
quote_note: The New York Times report (UPI) on Frank Rosenblatt's Perceptron.
who: US Navy, as reported by The New York Times (UPI)

quote_sources.title: "New Navy Device Learns by Doing" — The New York Times archive, 8 Jul 1958
Professor's perceptron paved the way for AI – 60 years too soon — Cornell Chronicle

happened: Cornell says Rosenblatt's perceptron paved the way for today's AI, about 60 years too soon. Machines now talk, see and write. Conscious? No evidence yet.

happened_sources.title: Cornell Chronicle, 25 Sep 2019

reason: Talk, see, write: yes. Reproduce itself and be conscious: not that anyone can show.

headline: MAIL BY GUIDED MISSILE, SAYS POSTMASTER
deck: A Navy missile carries 3,000 letters. The Postmaster General sees the future of the post.
quote: Before man reaches the moon, mail will be delivered within hours from New York to California, to Britain, to India or Australia by guided missiles.
who: Arthur E. Summerfield, US Postmaster General
where: Remarks on the 1959 Regulus missile-mail flight, as quoted by the Smithsonian National Postal Museum

quote_sources.title: Cruise Missile Mail — Smithsonian National Postal Museum

happened: The Smithsonian calls it the only time a missile was used to carry mail in the United States.

happened_sources.title: Cruise Missile Mail — Smithsonian National Postal Museum

reason: As ruled on air in Episode 3.
note: Aired episode: quote and source as published in the archive (Smithsonian page blocks automated fetches).

headline: A MAN ON THE MOON BEFORE THIS DECADE IS OUT
deck: The President asks Congress for the Moon, and a safe trip home.
quote: I believe that this nation should commit itself to achieving the goal, before this decade is out, of landing a man on the moon and returning him safely to the earth.
quote_note: A goal and a promise rather than a forecast.
where: Address to a joint session of Congress

quote_sources.title: Address to Joint Session of Congress, May 25, 1961 — JFK Library

happened: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969, and Apollo 11 came home safely.

happened_sources.title: Apollo 11 mission overview — NASA

reason: Done with five months of the decade to spare.
note: JFK Library quote checked via WebFetch on 11 Nov 2026.

headline: ROBOTS NEITHER COMMON NOR GOOD IN 2014
deck: Visiting the World's Fair, a science writer looks fifty years ahead.
quote: Robots will neither be common nor very good in 2014, but they will be in existence.

quote_sources.title: Visit to the World's Fair of 2014 — The New York Times

happened: iRobot says it has sold more than 50 million robots since the first Roomba in 2002.

happened_sources.title: iRobot fourth-quarter and full-year 2024 results

reason: As ruled on air in Episode 2.

headline: PAN AM: FIRST MOON FLIGHT EXPECTED IN 2000
deck: A journalist books a ticket to the Moon. The airline accepts.
quote: the first flight was expected to depart in 2000
quote_note: Pan Am's reported reply to a 1964 request for a Moon flight.

quote_sources.title: Were You a Member of the "First Moon Flights" Club? — Smithsonian NASM

happened: NASA's Artemis II crew flew around the Moon in April 2026, on a government mission. Still no tourist tickets.

happened_sources.title: NASA welcomes record-setting Artemis II Moonfarers back to Earth — NASA

episode_label: Episode 4: Pan Am to the Moon
reason: As ruled on air in Episode 4.

headline: CHIPS WILL BRING HOME COMPUTERS AND PORTABLE PHONES
deck: A chip engineer predicts components per chip will keep doubling, and lists the wonders to come.
quote: Integrated circuits will lead to such wonders as home computers—or at least terminals connected to a central computer—automatic controls for automobiles, and personal portable communications equipment.
where: "Cramming more components onto integrated circuits", Electronics

quote_sources.title: Cramming more components onto integrated circuits (Electronics, 1965) — PDF, Georgia Tech

happened: His doubling rule became "Moore's Law", which the Computer History Museum calls one of the driving principles of the chip industry.

happened_sources.title: 1965: "Moore's Law" predicts the future of integrated circuits — Computer History Museum

reason: Home computers, car electronics and mobile phones, all in one sentence.

headline: MOON BASE AND MEN ON MARS BEFORE 2000
deck: Eighty-two scientists asked by the RAND Corporation agree on a busy century in space.
quote: In Rand's Delphi study, 82 scientists agreed that a permanent lunar base will have been established long before A.D. 2000 and that men will have flown past Venus and landed on Mars.
quote_note: Time's summary of the RAND study.
who: 82 scientists in a RAND Corporation study, as reported by Time

quote_sources.title: "The Futurists: Looking Toward A.D. 2000" — Time, 25 Feb 1966

happened: No Moon base and no one on Mars yet. NASA says it is working to send astronauts to Mars "as early as the 2030s".

happened_sources.title: Humans to Mars — NASA

reason: Both are still on the to-do list.
note: Time quote checked in the fetched Time archive page (WebFetch) on 11 Nov 2026.

headline: SHOPPING FROM HOME WILL FLOP, SAY SKEPTICS
deck: The futurists picture shopping by video phone. Others are sure nobody will want it.
quote: ...remote shopping, while entirely feasible, will flop—because women like to get out of the house, like to handle the merchandise, like to be able to change their minds.
quote_note: Time's summary of what the skeptics among the futurists said, not a named person's words.
who: Skeptics among the futurists, as summed up by Time

quote_sources.title: "The Futurists: Looking Toward A.D. 2000" — Time, 25 Feb 1966

happened: E-commerce was 16.4% of all US retail sales in the second quarter of 2026, according to the US Census Bureau.

happened_sources.title: Quarterly retail e-commerce sales — US Census Bureau

reason: Remote shopping did not flop. (The reasoning has not aged well either.)
note: Time quote checked in the fetched Time archive page (WebFetch) on 11 Nov 2026.

headline: HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS WILL STARVE IN THE 1970s
deck: A best-selling biologist says the battle to feed humanity is already lost.
quote: The battle to feed all of humanity is over... In the 1970s... hundreds of millions of people are going to starve to death.
quote_note: Two passages joined, as quoted by Smithsonian Magazine.

quote_sources.title: The Book That Incited a Worldwide Fear of Overpopulation — Smithsonian Magazine

happened: Famines still kill, but Our World in Data shows famine deaths fell sharply over the second half of the 20th century, calling it one of the great accomplishments of our era.

happened_sources.title: Famines — Our World in Data

reason: The mass starvation he forecast for the 1970s did not happen on anything like that scale.

headline: MAN ON MARS WITHIN 15 YEARS, SAYS SPACE PANEL
deck: Weeks after Apollo 11, the White House space panel says NASA can do it.
quote: We conclude that NASA has the demonstrated organizational competence and technology base, by virtue of the Apollo success and other achievements, to carry out a successful program to land man on Mars within 15 years.
who: The Space Task Group (chaired by Vice-President Spiro Agnew)
where: "The Post-Apollo Space Program: Directions for the Future"

quote_sources.title: Space Task Group Report, 1969 — NASA History
"Manned Mars Landing", von Braun briefing, Aug 1969 — NASA Technical Reports Server

happened: No one has landed on Mars. NASA now aims for "as early as the 2030s".

happened_sources.title: Humans to Mars — NASA

reason: The 15 years ran out in 1984. Mars is still waiting.

headline: EVERY HOME WILL HAVE A COMPUTER CONSOLE BY 2001
deck: Standing among room-sized machines, a writer describes your child's future.
quote: ...he will have, in his own house, not a computer as big as this, but at least a console through which he can talk to his friendly local computer and get all the information he needs for his everyday life like his bank statements, his theater reservations...

quote_sources.title: Arthur C Clarke's computer prediction in 1974 — ABC News (video)
Tech Time Warp: Arthur C. Clarke predicts the internet, 1974 — WIRED

happened: 5.5 billion people, 68% of the world, were online in 2024, says the ITU.

reason: Online banking and booking from home, described 20 years before the web went mainstream.

headline: MILLIONS WILL WORK FROM HOME
deck: A futurist predicts the "electronic cottage", where jobs move back into the house.

happened: The number of Americans mainly working from home tripled from 2019 to 2021, to 27.6 million people (17.9% of workers), says the US Census Bureau.

happened_sources.title: The Number of People Primarily Working From Home Tripled Between 2019 and 2021 — US Census Bureau, 15 Sep 2022

reason: Literally millions, though it took a pandemic to make it happen at scale.

headline: ROBOTS WILL MOVE INTO THE HOME BY 2019
deck: Asked to picture 2019, a science writer sees computers and robots everywhere.

happened: iRobot says it has sold more than 50 million robots since 2002, almost all floor cleaners. General-purpose home robots are still at the pre-order stage.

happened_sources.title: iRobot fourth-quarter and full-year 2024 results
NEO home robot — 1X

reason: Robots did get into the home, but mostly to vacuum it.

headline: HOME COMPUTERS WILL BE FOR GETTING ONLINE

headline: A TALKING ASSISTANT IN A FOLDING COMPUTER

headline: BY 2013, A ROBOT WILL COOK, CLEAN AND DO THE WASHING

headline: A COMPUTER WILL BE CHESS CHAMPION BEFORE THE 1990S ARE OUT
